A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the amplitude of the AP is not a reliable indicator of the presence or absence of endolymph in the scala vestibuli, and that the presence of a SP does not prove that the scala tympani is also filled with endolymph.
the SP/AP ratio is a useful measure for detecting endolymphatic fluid pressure abnormalities, but the SP/AP ratio should be used with caution in interpreting the nature of the abnormality.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a tympanic membrane probe is an excellent tool for evaluating cochlear function in the clinical setting.
electrocochleographic response patterns are complex and that the use of alternating polarity click stimuli alone is insufficient to fully characterize these patterns.
a variety of response abnormalities occur in patients with endolymphatic disorders and these can be revealed by the use of condensation and rarefaction polarity clicks.
